title: createClient tree-shaking
body:
`import { createClient } from "@openauthjs/openauth";` 

fails on the client (nextjs) because it has a transitive dependency `node:crypto` via `hono` via the root import. Next does not polyfill `node:crypto` on purpose (?).

```
Module build failed: UnhandledSchemeError: Reading from "node:crypto" is not handled by plugins (Unhandled scheme).
Webpack supports "data:" and "file:" URIs by default.
You may need an additional plugin to handle "node:" URIs.
Import trace for requested module:
node:crypto
./node_modules/.pnpm/hono@4.6.13/node_modules/hono/dist/adapter/aws-lambda/handler.js
./node_modules/.pnpm/hono@4.6.13/node_modules/hono/dist/adapter/aws-lambda/index.js
./node_modules/.pnpm/@openauthjs+openauth@0.0.20_arctic@2.3.0_hono@4.6.13/node_modules/@openauthjs/openauth/dist/esm/authorizer.js
./node_modules/.pnpm/@openauthjs+openauth@0.0.20_arctic@2.3.0_hono@4.6.13/node_modules/@openauthjs/openauth/dist/esm/index.js
```
Instead, this works -- 

`import { createClient } from "@openauthjs/openauth/client";`.

Not a critical issue, but maybe a UX one getting started.

title: Add login OTP logic for password
body:
This adds the ability for the password provider to generate an OTP (optional) when the client logs in, that the client has to then provide accurately.

The `generateOtp` function gets req and email and can return an OTP. Up to the implementor to decide whether an OTP is required based on req+email.

This does add a slight breaking change to the API, could create a separate provider `password-otp` instead.
Or, we could rename the new callback that takes state to `authorize` instead of `login`, and leave the old callback so that old implementations still work.
author: ajoslin

comments.body: Please let me know if you prefer the breaking change or to make the new callback that takes `state` have a new name like `authorize`.

so the way i had imagined this was by composing different providers together.

in the `success` callback for password, you could save a cookie with their info and then redirect them to code auth.
and then in success for the code provider, you retreive their info and log them in

Hmmm, yeah, clearly superior way to do it because it would allow OTP for all provider types.
